hook: Ellsworth graduated early from Stanford with a B.S. in Computer Science with Distinction, worked as a research engineer at Google DeepMind, and now leads initiatives related to search and agents as a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI. He was a U.S. Presidential Scholar and a USA Biology Olympiad national finalist.
name: Will Ellsworth

quote.text: Graduated early from Stanford University with a B.S. in Computer Science and now doing fun AI stuff.

reading.body:
OpenAI's search and agent work is led by someone who moved there directly from Google DeepMind after proving himself as a research engineer, suggesting both labs are competing for the same narrow pool of top-tier talent in frontier AI.

Ellsworth's path tracks the consolidation of AI research talent toward the largest labs. He entered the field with elite credentials, moved to DeepMind as a research engineer, then shifted to OpenAI as a member of technical staff within two years. The speed of that transition and his rapid elevation to leading initiatives on search and agents indicates these roles are not entry-level. His focus on agents and search are compute-intensive domains that will reshape how users interact with AI systems.

What this record does not show is how many researchers at his level move between the major labs each year, or how OpenAI and Google DeepMind's compensation and working conditions compare. It also does not reveal whether his departure from DeepMind reflects a strategic decision by one lab or a pull from another. The data confirms only that building frontier AI systems requires recruiting researchers of this caliber and that these researchers are actively moving between the organizations that compete to scale compute.
